chronicle.text: Lakoukeim gathered food that had grown where seeds had been dropped: the first harvest from seed left in the ground.
Shebeibal came back for food left 25 weeks before, and it was still there.
Mokeban tied fiber and fiber together with fiber and was left with something to carry things in: the first carrier.
Sainei survived an attack by wolves.
Vaihe went back to what they had left in one spot a third time, to see it happen again: the first deliberate testing.
Sozais tied wood and wood together with fiber and was left with something that floats and carries someone across water: the first raft.
Sozais scratched a mark <\^v> into wood.
Mokeban drank from the sea and it did not quench their thirst.
Shebeibal set food aside on purpose, having found it there when it was needed before: the beginning of keeping stores.
At (8, 27) the heap of things people had left grew big enough to keep out a fifth of the winter cold: the first dwelling. Shebeibal had put in the most.
Kushul found that what Shebeibal had told them was wrong, and trusted them less for it.
Lakoukeim buried seed on purpose, having seen it come back as food: the beginning of farming.
Geizeikel tied stone and wood together with fiber and was left with something heavy on a handle: the first club.
Todel struck stone with flint and stared at what happened.
Todel struck flint with flint and was left with a sharp edge: the first blade.
Devuken tied a club and a wood flake together with fiber and was left with something warm to wear: the first wrap.
Dedis struck flint where dry things lay, and they caught: the first fire made by people.
Tasar tied a blade and wood together with fiber and was left with a sharp point on a long shaft: the first spear.
